title: Human–AI intellectual symbiosis from ordinary use through exceptional and speculative frontier capability
question: How do ordinary people, effective practitioners, specialists, and rare human–AI collaborators differ; what explains their results; and how could we demystify, learn and surpass their capabilities?

models.name: Two independent axes
models.statement: Observed achievement and transferable collaboration competence should not be inferred from one another.

models.name: Capability composition
models.statement: Problem selection, domain expertise, interaction, tools, evaluators, coordination and revision may interact; their contribution varies by task.

models.name: Distribution and conditional ranks
models.statement: Ordinary, 90th, 99th, and 99.9th strata are explicit research targets; they are not factual ranks without a reference population, task distribution and outcome measurements.

models.name: Legend-to-mechanism reduction
models.statement: An impressive achievement should be explained via a causal workflow, artifacts, prior expertise, resource constraints, failures, simpler reconstructions and transfer tests; unexplained residuals stay explicit.

models.name: Within-person and across-person transfer
models.statement: A working method in one tool, project or domain need not transfer to others; practical capability requires repeated success beyond the original example.

evidence_notes.observation: Alpöge's original announcement describes his role in selecting analogies and mathematical directions, and Claude contributing unexpected further steps. The proof claim was being examined at publication.
evidence_notes.interpretation: Promising example of expert steering with extensive AI exploration; effectiveness and correctness not established merely by the announcement.

evidence_notes.observation: DeepMind describes model-generated code, automated execution/scoring, and evolutionary selection; reports production deployment of several algorithmic improvements.
evidence_notes.interpretation: A plausible demonstration that model generation and reliable evaluators form a useful compound capability.

evidence_notes.observation: METR reports early-2025 experienced open-source developers took 19% longer when AI tools were available; a later study had substantial selection and measurement limitations.
evidence_notes.interpretation: Productivity depends on tasks, tools, practitioner context and measurement; cannot be inferred from tool use alone.

evidence_notes.observation: OpenAI Signals v3.0 describes sampled individual ChatGPT use through September 2026, excluding enterprise and Codex. Anthropic's January 2026 Economic Index classifies Claude usage by task, interaction and estimated success; it reports November 2025 augmentation at 52% and automated use at 45% on Claude.ai.
evidence_notes.interpretation: These anchor usage landscapes, but do not assign intellectual capability percentiles, nor establish that collaboration causes better outcomes.

evidence_notes.observation: The existing Knowledge Tree Navigator collaboration shows source-linked design, repository commits, bug reports (including trailing-slash API 404), a mistaken edit to Discord-Wiki and subsequent recovery.
evidence_notes.interpretation: A concrete workflow for analyzing human–AI symbiosis end-to-end; determine benefits and costs from the actual artifacts before any tier attribution.

evidence_notes.observation: OpenAI Signals and Anthropic Economic Index characterize ordinary use and interaction categories; SF Fed records business-use narratives; HBS reports owner Andy Brown built operational apps; Harvard controlled study evaluates a tailored AI tutor.
evidence_notes.basis: fieldwork.json cases FW-OPENAI, FW-CLAUDE, FW-SMALLBUS, FW-ANDY, FW-STUDENTS
evidence_notes.interpretation: AI use spans many environments and knowledge levels. Aggregate message distributions and isolated stories cannot establish population percentiles or general superiority.

evidence_notes.observation: Carlini chose parallel agents for separable compiler tasks and invested heavily in evaluators; Mishra-Sharma's coupled numerical solver was better suited to mostly sequential debugging against CLASS.
evidence_notes.interpretation: Hypothesis: coupling among tasks and quality of the evaluator, not number of agents, govern effective orchestration. This contrast is not itself a controlled test.

evidence_notes.observation: Found working primary artifacts: Showboat/Rodney, mini-swe-agent, DSPy, Claude C compiler, clax. Communities include Hugging Face, Latent Space, Lean and AI engineering talks.
evidence_notes.interpretation: These are candidate FKEN gas resources and practical scaffolding, not proof of acquired tacit competence.

candidate_probes.experiment: On a representative existing repository issue, compare an unassisted baseline with assisted work on a matched, similarly complex task. Count integration, debugging, verification and rework, not just text generation.
candidate_probes.discriminates: Whether AI improves real task completion under fixed quality requirements.

candidate_probes.experiment: Have one model generate candidate solutions for a measurable programming problem; then compare no evaluation, hand review, and executable evaluator with iteration.
candidate_probes.discriminates: Whether evaluator-driven search is a useful source of improvement instead of merely increasing generated volume.

candidate_probes.experiment: Return after a week to a new task in the same family and attempt to reuse saved problem representations, decision records and tests without replaying the entire chat.
candidate_probes.discriminates: Whether collaboration leaves transferable capability and durable working knowledge.

candidate_probes.experiment: Construct comparable task sets and evidence records for everyday, independent technical, expert specialist and institutional users. Observe actual outcomes and resource costs, not message frequency alone.
candidate_probes.discriminates: Whether broad user capability strata persist after controlling for task, expertise and access.

candidate_probes.experiment: Analyze the real Knowledge Tree Viewer development: identify parent purpose, each requested change, code alteration, test evidence, 404 regression, mistaken-target change, reversal, and time/rework.
candidate_probes.discriminates: Which aspects of this user's collaboration are generative versus friction or hidden overhead.

candidate_probes.experiment: From a published high-achievement case, reconstruct the minimal mechanism using ordinary tools on a smaller but representative problem; compare against a simpler baseline.
candidate_probes.discriminates: Whether the admired result depends on an accessible technique, niche expertise, expensive compute, or their composition.

next_question: Investigate how two existing exceptional but different AI collaborations work (Carlini parallel compiler versus Mishra-Sharma coupled numerical solver), then relate their mechanisms to ordinary and independent workflows; acquire evidence before assigning percentile ranks.

population_sampling.calibration_rule: Do not assign actual percentile ranks to people or workflows based on a few anecdotes. Define a reference population, a task family, a measure of independently verified performance or capability and a representative sample first.
sampling_axes: accessibility for novice, skilled individual, specialist or institution
biases_to_watch: model generation confounded with human expertise
apparently simple prompts hiding extensive preparation

demystification_contract.purpose: Replace reverence for an outcome or person with inspectable mechanisms, evidence and reproducible capabilities. Preserve real differences in expertise and resources.
case_questions: What problem did this person actually choose, and why?
What was already known or prepared before AI entered?
Exactly what did the human ask, decide, reject, test, revise and contribute?
What did the model produce and what could it do without the human?
Which tools, references, infrastructure, collaborators and prior expertise were essential?
How many failed approaches, retries and intermediate steps occurred?
What was observed, checked and independently reproduced?
What would the simplest lower-resource reconstruction look like?
Which capability can a capable beginner learn, which requires deliberate practice and which requires deep domain expertise?
What remains unexplained or currently inaccessible, and what evidence would resolve it?
demystification_contract.anti_myth_rule: Do not replace a legend with a simplistic 'anyone can do it' story. Distinguish replicable method, expertise, unusually favorable problem selection, institution-scale resources and unexplained residuals.

case_study_contract.starting_question: If we remove the person's name and reputation, what did they actually do?
case_study_contract.completion_rule: A case is not demystified merely by a fluent summary or an impressive resulting artifact. Require checkable mechanisms and a feasible independent competence probe; preserve unavailable evidence.

fieldwork_status: 14 source-linked cases covering everyday work and learning, working engineers, scientific systems, frontier claims and counterexamples; empirical percentile assignment unresolved

method_revision.what_changed: First comparative investigation through documentary samples, not speculative ranking. Each case records observed workflow, competing mechanism hypotheses, remaining uncertainty and cheap reconstruction probes.
method_revision.relevance: Cases inform multiple questions without turning the question tree into a celebrity list.

fieldwork_link_rule: fieldwork_case_ids point to source-backed records in fieldwork_path; follow them for mechanism explanations, action traces, limitations and original sources. Case links are not completed proof certificates.
